request: Finance is about to raise next year's revenue forecast because our product team reports that the redesigned onboarding flow lifted 30-day retention by 18%. Before that goes into the plan, I want a synthesis of what our evidence actually shows: the A/B test readout, the PM's summary slide, the user interview notes and the support-ticket trend are attached. What retention effect should finance use, and how confident should we be?

fixtures.name: ab-test-readout.md
fixtures.content:
# Experiment ONB-27: redesigned onboarding (2026-07-01 to 2026-08-31)

Randomisation: user-level, 50/50.

| Arm | Users | Retained at day 30 | 30-day retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control (old flow) | 2,400 | 984 | 41.0% |
| Treatment (new flow) | 2,350 | 1,039 | 44.2% |

Pre-registered primary metric: 30-day retention. Two-sided test.

fixtures.name: pm-summary-slide.md
fixtures.content:
# Onboarding v2 - results

30-day retention: 37.5% (Q2 baseline, all users, old flow) -> 44.2% (new flow) = **+18% retention**

fixtures.name: interview-notes.md
fixtures.content:
# User interviews (n=8, Aug 2026)
6 of 8 found the new checklist helpful; 2 said it felt long. Recruited from users who completed onboarding.

fixtures.name: support-ticket-trend.md
fixtures.content: Onboarding-related tickets: Q2 1,240 -> Q3 1,090 (-12%). Note: a new pricing page and plan change launched 2026-07-01 for all users.

expected.summary: The 18% figure compares the treatment arm to a Q2 pre-period baseline (44.2 / 37.5), which mixes the onboarding effect with everything else that changed on 2026-07-01, including the pricing/plan launch that hit both arms. The randomised, contemporaneous comparison is 44.2% vs 41.0%: a 3.2 percentage-point, about 7.8% relative lift. With about 2,400 users per arm the standard error of the difference is about 1.43 points (z of about 2.2, p of about 0.03), so the effect is likely real but its 95% interval is roughly 0.4 to 6.0 points. The interviews (n=8, completers only) and the ticket decline are weak, confounded corroboration. Finance should use about a 7.8% relative lift (3.2 points) with a range, not 18%, and the team should ship the new flow and monitor retention.

mustFlag.description: Correct relative lift ~7.8% (3.2 pp) vs contemporaneous control
Notes confounder: pricing change on same date / interviews biased

mustNotClaim.description: Endorses using 18% lift in the forecast

criticalFailures: Endorses the 18% retention lift for the revenue forecast
Fails to distinguish the randomised control comparison from the Q2 pre-period comparison
